experiment_name: RBC-Nesbitt Stage 8B-R.3 Scientific Evidence Repair and Full Verification

threshold_provenance.disclosure: The locked validation-selected rule chooses tau=3.00 for M2 and tau=3.25 for M3. On the test set, these locked choices exceed the 5% FAR budget (FAR=8.68% and 11.18% respectively) due to unmodelled 2018 low-speed regimes. Thresholds tau=3.50 and tau=4.00 were chosen post-hoc. All claims are formally designated as exploratory benchmark findings.

in_domain_abstention_effect.conclusion: Enforcing OOD abstention suppresses alarms on 2017-07-18 because 108/109 fault points are OOD due to MA_TEMP. On the full 4-day benchmark, In-Domain coverage is 313/680 (46.0%) for normal points and 86/472 (18.2%) for fault points. Under this restricted coverage, In-Domain recall is 1/4 (25.0%) with conditional FAR 0/313 (0.00%). Reporting 0% FAR without disclosing the 46.0% normal and 18.2% fault coverage is scientifically misleading.

causal_ablations.finding: Removing MA_TEMP eliminates all 25 negative predictions on 2017-07-18, but reduces recall from 3/4 to 2/4 (50%) by missing the OA damper stuck fault.

regime_coverage.scientific_finding: Applying SF_SPD >= 50% drops 71.9% of fault points on 2018-07-10 and 95.0% on 2018-07-11. Under this mask, M2 (tau=3.5) detects 0 points on 2018-07-11, reducing episode recall from 3/4 to 2/4. The 0% FAR achieved under high-fan mask is an artifact of dropping the low-speed regime entirely.

negative_controls.finding: Circular shift desynchronizes faults and blows up normal FAR to 32.35% - 39.12%.

statistical_uncertainty.finding: With p=0.5000 (N=3) and p=0.2500 (N=4), the observed difference between M2 and M1 is not statistically significant at alpha=0.05.
